cells.tense: The momentum is being aimed from what feels alive, and it is holding its line today.
cells.ask: Name one thing you feel a pull toward, out loud, and name the next small move on it — say both to one person who will ask about them again later.
cells.core:
You're moving toward something with a real feel behind it, and that's why the direction holds. The pull is genuine and it steers the effort without needing to be justified first — aim and appetite are pointed the same way, which is less common than either one alone.

Keep it there by feeding what you actually feel, not what you think you're meant to feel. When a turn is open and nothing in you moves, letting it stay open is part of it. A drive like this doesn't need a shove behind it; it needs what you feel kept legible, so the aim stays true and the road stays worth taking.
cells.sheetLine: You're aiming from what you feel, and it's holding.
cells.verb: Steering by what can be felt and fully imagined
cells.place: In the part of life where energy is aimed at a destination

cells.tense: You will be rushing the arrival before what is here has been fully felt.
cells.ask: Pick one thing already going well and tend it by hand for a day: water it, mend it, or clear what's crowding it, and stop there — with no push for it to grow faster than it is.
cells.core:
Running well, the drive comes out of what you've already lived through. You want a thing because you've felt your way through it, so the pace is the pace of real things and you arrive when you arrive rather than pushing the whole way there.

Happening now: a grip on the finish line. A completed version sits in your head and you keep sprinting toward it before the part that's here has been felt, forcing the pace past what a thing needs to take shape. The hurry is spending energy headed for a result that may still be far off.

What's already growing doesn't need to be rushed. Care without force is the whole of it. Stay near, tend it, let it set its own time, so the drive stays yours and the road doesn't hollow you out.

cells.tense: The aiming stopped back when something you felt strongly didn't turn out, and the stillness held.
cells.ask: Write three sentences about something you care enough about to want: what it is, what it would change, and one reason you'd want it — keep the sentences plain and show them to no one unless you choose to.
cells.core:
Working well, the aim starts from what you've already felt your way through. You want a thing because you've been in it, so the push comes from inside what you feel rather than from outside pressure, and the direction lands without argument and holds without strain.

The pointing has stopped. You know what you want here and you're not saying it or moving on it — the still spot where you stand is one you'd recognise, and what you know hasn't gone anywhere. The pointing did.

The aim isn't gone. It's waiting on the charge you used to spend on wanting itself. Let what you know say one plain thing first, before any move is needed, so the current returns through the aim from the other side.
cells.sheetLine: You know what you want. You've stopped aiming at it.

cells.tense: The direction is running right now, in choices and daily moves you're calling just how things are.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one thing you keep reaching for is yours — the workouts, the savings, the way you keep showing up — and say what it's for, with no one casual in the room and no permission asked.
cells.core:
Working well, the aim is owned. You feel the pull, you've said what it's for, and the daily moves line up with what you want instead of being driven by something you can't name. The direction holds because you chose it and can say so.

The same aim is running now while you describe it as just how things are. The agenda has destinations in it, and the small moves order the day around something you want — but the direction gets talked about as temporary, given, not chosen. The steering is happening; owning it is not.

You picked what to steer by. Saying that doesn't change the aim; it puts the hand back on the wheel. Own the move and the strength you spend stops being a habit you can't name and becomes a choice you set.
cells.sheetLine: You're aimed at something. You call it just how things are.
cells.verb: Steering by what can be felt and fully imagined
